Nuclear-risk interpretations should not be treated as proof of personal intent.","closed_system_silence":"High residual risk because classified command, safety, and arsenal information is inaccessible; the notebook explicitly identifies missing technical follow-up.","duplicate_reporting":"Several nuclear claims derive from the same Bulletin, IAEA, or official-policy materials; they should not be counted as independent corroboration.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both are present: official deterrence and stability claims are recorded alongside escalation, verification loss, and safety concerns.","missing_source_type":"Later-2023 IAEA follow-up and a fully inspected technical assessment of Russian nuclear forces and command safety are missing.","official_claim_independence":"Official Russian and Belarusian claims are included but independently checked against FAS and FOI assessments; physical deployment remains unresolved.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not a principal risk for this chapter; public complaint volume is not the main evidence base.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Strategic exposure and inherited 2022 conditions are addressed, but population-level exposure, baseline force posture, and wartime external shocks are only partly developed.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-1B-01","WEB-1B-02","WEB-1B-03","WEB-1B-05","WEB-1B-06","WEB-1B-R1-20260805-A01","WEB-1B-R1-20260805-A02","WEB-1B-R1-20260805-A03","WEB-1B-R1-20260805-A04","WEB-1B-R1-20260805-A05"],"unresolved_risks":["The 1B.9 evidence covers AI and radiation safety but not a comprehensive 2023 cyber, biological, or dual-use safeguards framework.","IAEA coverage ends early in 2023 and later operational conduct remains insufficiently documented.","The notebook contains discovery-only candidates, including WEB-1B-07, WEB-1B-08, and WEB-1B-12."]},"chapter_id":"1B","defensible_evidence_estimate":9,"independent_source_family_estimate":8,"missing_themes":["Later-2023 nuclear-plant safety and safeguards follow-up","Verified Russian nuclear-force posture and command-safety evidence","Russia-specific 2023 cyber, biological, and dual-use catastrophic-risk governance"],"substantive_issues":["Several claims are later retrospectives or inherited-baseline evidence rather than full-period observations.","The evidence supports institutional and policy attribution more strongly than personal operational responsibility.","A credible technical source remains only a discovery candidate, so the principal missing themes are research-recoverable but unresolved."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"The notebook generally distinguishes UN findings, ICC reasonable-grounds allegations, official denials, and policy analysis. ICC material is not a conviction and must remain at that evidentiary stage.","closed_system_silence":"High: restricted access to Russian-controlled detention sites and wartime censorship may conceal violations and suppress contrary evidence.","duplicate_reporting":"OHCHR, UN Commission, ICRC, Carnegie, and ICC materials overlap on the war and detention context; repeated casualty and conduct descriptions may represent the same underlying events.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both are present: humanitarian access, prisoner visits, exchanges, and Russian legal justifications appear alongside findings of unlawful attacks, detention, torture, and failed settlement.","missing_source_type":"Direct command records, Russian-controlled-site access, and independent judicial or investigative records concerning attribution and remedy are missing.","official_claim_independence":"Russian claims are reported as contrary evidence but are not independently substantiated; UN and ICRC materials provide stronger external checks.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open reporting and monitoring can overrepresent accessible or high-profile incidents, while restricted areas likely produce undercounting; the notebook acknowledges both directions.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Civilian and POW exposure, inherited 2022 conditions, Russian authority, and war-related external shocks are addressed, but 2023-only denominators and comprehensive population coverage remain incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-2B-01","WEB-2B-02","WEB-2B-03","WEB-2B-04","WEB-2B-05","WEB-2B-06","WEB-2B-07","WEB-2B-09","WEB-2B-10","WEB-2B-R1-20260805-A01","WEB-2B-R1-20260805-A02","WEB-2B-R1-20260805-A03","WEB-2B-R1-20260805-A04","WEB-2B-R1-20260805-A05"],"unresolved_risks":["Many findings cover cumulative periods beginning in 2022 and cannot be treated as 2023-only.","Russian institutional attribution is substantially stronger than direct personal attribution for battlefield and detention conduct.","The notebook includes candidate material not fully opened, including the Olenivka report."]},"chapter_id":"2B","defensible_evidence_estimate":13,"independent_source_family_estimate":9,"missing_themes":["Direct evidence linking senior command decisions to specific 2023 battlefield or detention incidents","Complete 2023-only event chronology and denominators","Independent evidence from Russian-controlled detention sites and effective remedies"],"substantive_issues":["High volume does not equal proportional coverage because many entries repeat broad war facts or share source families.","The strongest personal attribution is limited to the ICC’s stated reasonable-grounds responsibility concerning child transfers; other conduct remains institutional or policy-level.","Candidate breadth and access limitations leave some event-specific contrary evidence unresolved."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Case reports and rights-monitoring findings are generally distinguished from official justifications. Political-prisoner and enforced-disappearance characterizations retain stated uncertainty.","closed_system_silence":"Very high: censorship, prison opacity, restricted access, and intimidation can suppress evidence of abuse and accountability failures.","duplicate_reporting":"HRW, Amnesty, OVD-Info, and Carnegie overlap on repression, Navalny, and Wagner; repeated descriptions should be consolidated by underlying fact.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both are present: formal legal prohibitions, courts, continuing dissent, and restored federal control are recorded alongside torture, repression, prison abuse, and coercive laws.","missing_source_type":"Independent domestic legal, prison-inspection, judicial, and official complaint-resolution records are missing or inaccessible.","official_claim_independence":"Official claims are recorded as contrary evidence, but independent verification of prison administration and state security explanations is limited.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Complaint and monitoring counts may be biased toward visible cases and accessible victims, while closed institutions likely cause substantial undercounting.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Affected groups and national legal authority are addressed; inherited post-invasion conditions and wartime shocks are noted, but prevalence and regional exposure are not established.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-3B-02","WEB-3B-03","WEB-3B-04","WEB-3B-05","WEB-3B-06","WEB-3B-07","WEB-3B-08"],"unresolved_risks":["Two selected lenses have explicit local evidence gaps.","Several reports concern inherited conditions beginning in 2022 rather than conduct confined to 2023.","Blocked UN candidates could materially improve torture, detention, and occupation attribution."]},"chapter_id":"3B","defensible_evidence_estimate":7,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Independent 2023 UN evidence on detention, torture, and occupation conduct","Prison oversight, complaint handling, and remedy outcomes","Systematic regional or population-level prevalence of coercive treatment"],"substantive_issues":["The available evidence is strong for state policy and institutional conduct but weaker for direct presidential direction or knowledge in individual cases.","Access-blocked UN sources are credible and potentially material, so the dossier is not fully saturated.","Visible opposition cases may not represent the broader affected population."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Election-monitoring observations, legal acts, and court or administrative events are distinguished from evaluative conclusions about fairness. Official security rationales are retained as contrary evidence.","closed_system_silence":"High: restrictions on media, observers, civil society, and independent organizations limit detection of irregularities and retaliation.","duplicate_reporting":"Golos entries substantially overlap on the September elections, candidate registration, and administrative mobilization; Freedom House, HRW, Amnesty, and RSF also share broader repression facts.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both are present: opposition candidates, regional exceptions, domestic observation, and functioning formal institutions are recorded alongside controlled competition, censorship, and exclusion.","missing_source_type":"Complete official election files, precinct-level results, independent domestic observer data, and accessible digital-sphere evidence are missing.","official_claim_independence":"Official rationales are checked against Golos, OSCE/ODIHR, Meduza, RSF, and rights reporting, but OSCE access was itself restricted.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open monitoring may emphasize observable contested regions and opposition complaints; repression and restricted observation can simultaneously suppress reporting.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Voters, candidates, media, and regional variation are addressed; inherited institutional conditions and wartime/security shocks are present, but population-wide exposure is incompletely measured.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-4B-01","WEB-4B-02","WEB-4B-03","WEB-4B-04","WEB-4B-05","WEB-4B-06","WEB-4B-07","WEB-4B-08"],"unresolved_risks":["Access-blocked Freedom on the Net and electoral-dynamics sources could improve digital and competition coverage.","The evidence establishes national and institutional responsibility more securely than Putin’s personal involvement in local irregularities.","Some evidence is retrospective or concerns inherited conditions."]},"chapter_id":"4B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["Precinct-level and official-result verification for 2023 elections","Independent digital-media and internet-restriction evidence","Direct evidence of presidential knowledge or direction of local electoral irregularities"],"substantive_issues":["Several Golos claims are distinct observations from one monitoring family and should not be treated as fully independent.","The evidence is adequate for national policy-level attribution but not for every subordinate or regional event.","Access-blocked candidate sources leave a material, research-recoverable information gap."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Macroeconomic figures, regulatory actions, and budget assessments are separated from interpretations of welfare and sustainability. Official performance claims are qualified by independent World Bank and budget-transparency material.","closed_system_silence":"Medium-high: classified wartime spending and reduced disclosure can hide distributional costs, procurement inefficiency, and fiscal trade-offs.","duplicate_reporting":"Most economic claims repeat the Bank of Russia Annual Report; multiple entries are not independent source families and should be deduplicated.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both are present: GDP recovery, financial resilience, consumer protections, and sanctions adaptation are balanced against inflation, over-indebtedness, labor shortages, secrecy, and structural costs.","missing_source_type":"Accessible independent national statistics, household surveys, regional distributional data, and a fully inspected monetary-policy framework are missing.","official_claim_independence":"Bank of Russia claims receive partial checks from World Bank and IBP, but many outcomes remain dependent on official data and self-reporting.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not a primary source of evidence; household and consumer effects may be underrepresented where surveys or complaints are unavailable.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Aggregate outcomes, poverty/distribution context, sanctions, wartime spending, and delegated central-bank authority are addressed, but household and regional exposure remains incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-5B-01","WEB-5B-02","WEB-5B-03","WEB-5B-04","WEB-5B-05","WEB-5B-06","WEB-5B-07","WEB-5B-08","WEB-5B-09","WEB-5B-10"],"unresolved_risks":["The notebook explicitly reports failed access to Rosstat GDP data, AP household reporting, and the full monetary-policy framework.","Two selected lenses have explicit local evidence gaps.","Wartime growth is difficult to separate from external sanctions, commodity conditions, and defense spending."]},"chapter_id":"5B","defensible_evidence_estimate":6,"independent_source_family_estimate":4,"missing_themes":["Independent verification of GDP, inflation, and regional distributional outcomes","Household-level welfare and poverty effects","Transparent accounting of wartime fiscal and defense-spending trade-offs"],"substantive_issues":["The chapter is heavily dependent on one official Bank of Russia source, so its high observation count overstates independence.","Candidate Rosstat, Treasury, Accounts Chamber, AP, and IMF materials remain incompletely integrated or inspected.","Macro resilience cannot by itself establish broad welfare or effective policy performance."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"The available material mostly consists of official announcements, international indicators, and broad scholarly context. Announced inputs are correctly distinguished from delivered outcomes; causal attribution remains weak.","closed_system_silence":"High: official reporting and limited access to service-delivery records can conceal regional failures, exclusion, and unmet need.","duplicate_reporting":"UNICEF, WHO, World Bank, and Bank of Russia indicators describe related national conditions but are not all independent measures of service quality; the long-term synthesis is not 2023-specific.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both are present but uneven: mortality and financing claims are favorable, while missing service-access data, inflation, and uneven outcomes provide adverse or limiting evidence.","missing_source_type":"Primary 2023 benefit-execution, poverty, health-service delivery, regional-disparity, and audit records are missing or blocked.","official_claim_independence":"Government financing claims are partly checked by UNICEF, WHO, World Bank, and academic material, but implementation and outcome claims lack sufficient independent verification.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Complaint-volume evidence is absent; this prevents assessing whether reported service problems are overrepresented or suppressed.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"National mortality, economic conditions, long-term baselines, and shared federal/regional authority are addressed, but vulnerable-group and regional exposure is largely unresolved.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-6B-01","WEB-6B-02","WEB-6B-03","WEB-6B-04","WEB-6B-05","WEB-6B-06"],"unresolved_risks":["One selected lens has an explicit local evidence gap.","The Social Fund annual report, Rosstat poverty release, and Ministry of Health 2023 results were access-blocked.","Most evidence does not establish 2023 implementation quality or equitable access."]},"chapter_id":"6B","defensible_evidence_estimate":5,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["2023 poverty and inequality outcomes","Health-service delivery, access, quality, and regional variation","Execution and audit of benefits, insurance financing, and social programs"],"substantive_issues":["Announced funding is not evidence of effective or equitable delivery.","WHO and the scholarly synthesis are mainly baseline or longer-term context rather than target-period outcome evidence.","The blocked primary records are material and research-recoverable, so the chapter remains substantially under-evidenced."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"The notebook carefully distinguishes fact-checked public statements, sanctions or asset freezes, investigative allegations, proximity, and absence of criminal findings. Personal ownership or criminality is not established from network evidence alone.","closed_system_silence":"Very high: repression, secrecy, and constrained oversight can hide misconduct, beneficial ownership, retaliation, and failed remedies.","duplicate_reporting":"OCCRP and partner reports overlap on the same family, associate, and property networks; REPO and investigative reporting may describe related assets but are not automatically independent.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both are present: formal legality, official accountability claims, courts, and procedural institutions are recorded alongside disputed statements, asset freezes, patronage indicators, and oversight restrictions.","missing_source_type":"Primary beneficial-ownership records, domestic anti-corruption investigations, judicial findings, asset-forfeiture records, and accessible GRECO assessment are missing.","official_claim_independence":"Official rhetoric and sanctions statements are checked against Euronews, OCCRP, Meduza, and HRW, but official asset intelligence and Russian denials remain difficult to independently test.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Complaint and investigative volume is likely suppressed by repression; exposed elite cases may also be selected for visibility and political salience rather than population prevalence.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Elite networks, formal authority, oversight constraints, and inherited institutional conditions are addressed, but broader population exposure and external sanctions shocks are not central or fully developed.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-7B-01","WEB-7B-02","WEB-7B-03","WEB-7B-04","WEB-7B-05","WEB-7B-06","WEB-7B-07"],"unresolved_risks":["Seven selected lenses have explicit local evidence gaps.","Most network evidence is indirect and predates or spans beyond 2023.","Access-blocked GRECO, Supreme Court, and family-business materials could materially improve personal-integrity attribution."]},"chapter_id":"7B","defensible_evidence_estimate":4,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Direct 2023 personal-integrity findings concerning Putin","Primary beneficial-ownership and asset-control evidence","Independent anti-corruption oversight, investigation, and remedy outcomes"],"substantive_issues":["The dossier does not establish a sufficiently direct personal-integrity nexus for much of the network evidence.","Asset freezes and proximity evidence are not findings of criminal conduct or personal ownership.","The blocked source candidates are material, and the chapter is not adequate for fair personal attribution without substantial qualification."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Policy documents, macroeconomic outcomes, repression records, and strategic analyses are separated from interpretations of effectiveness. The notebook records both regime preservation and unresolved war, economic, and coordination problems.","closed_system_silence":"High: authoritarian information controls and wartime secrecy can conceal implementation failures, dissent, and adverse outcomes.","duplicate_reporting":"Bank of Russia and Carnegie materials recur across implementation, outcomes, and war-effectiveness claims; Wagner and repression entries also overlap with Chapters 2B-4B.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both are present: policy implementation, economic adaptation, regime continuity, and restored control are balanced against unresolved objectives, inflation, repression, and the Wagner control failure.","missing_source_type":"Independent program audits, complete government performance reporting, battlefield effectiveness assessments, and transparent outcome data are missing or blocked.","official_claim_independence":"Official policy and economic claims receive partial checks from Carnegie and OVD-Info, but several outcome claims remain based on official reporting or expert synthesis.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Public dissent and complaint indicators are suppressed by repression; surviving complaint or monitoring counts may overrepresent accessible cases and undercount closed-system harms.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Policy domains, state authority, inherited war conditions, sanctions, and external support are addressed, but population-level effects and counterfactual effectiveness are incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-8B-01","WEB-8B-02","WEB-8B-03","WEB-8B-04","WEB-8B-05","WEB-8B-06","WEB-8B-07","WEB-8B-08","WEB-8B-09","WEB-8B-10"],"unresolved_risks":["Two selected lenses have explicit local evidence gaps.","Blocked government and presidential performance materials could add direct implementation and correction evidence.","Economic adaptation and regime survival do not establish success against stated strategic objectives."]},"chapter_id":"8B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["Independent verification of implementation and outcome claims across policy domains","Battlefield and strategic-effectiveness evidence for 2023 objectives","Direct evidence of transparent correction or learning on core war assumptions"],"substantive_issues":["The chapter combines several distinct policy domains and relies heavily on recurring Bank of Russia and Carnegie sources.","Regime control is a measurable outcome but is not equivalent to broad policy effectiveness.","Access-blocked government and presidential records leave material attribution and execution gaps."]}],"global_findings":["Research rounds were exhausted without full saturation; this is a terminal research conclusion, not a claim that the dossier is complete.","All eight selected chapters were reviewed exactly once for the immutable selected lens scope.","The notebook contains substantial cited material, but defensible evidence is lower than raw fact-instance counts because repeated source-locator-claim units, gateway or discovery-only candidates, bundled claims, and shared source families must be excluded or consolidated.","Missing evidence was treated as an evidence gap, not as negative ruler evidence.","The principal recurring risks are institutional-to-personal attribution slippage, inherited or cumulative periods presented alongside 2023 evidence, dependence on official or repeated source families, restricted access in Russia and occupied areas, and incomplete contrary or population-level evidence.","Several chapters contain promising unfetched or access-blocked sources, but this terminal review does not request another continuation. Residual gaps are preserved for downstream confidence and interpretation."],"needs_continuation":false,"reviewer_summary":"Terminal no-search evidence-quality review completed for Chapters 1B-8B. The notebook provides meaningful multi-family evidence, but adequacy varies: Chapters 2B and 4B have substantial institutional evidence; Chapters 1B, 3B, 5B, and 8B retain material technical, access, independence, or attribution limitations; Chapter 6B is underdeveloped on 2023 delivery and distributional outcomes; and Chapter 7B has the greatest personal-integrity attribution risk. No scores or ranking recommendations are assigned.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":[]}
